clue.text: Drunk, the first lieutenant chose to go without

indicators.note: to go without here means to sit on the outside, so the word for chose wraps round the other piece

parts.note: picked means chose

indicators.note: the first points to the opening letter of the word lieutenant

explanation.surface: An officer who has had too much decides to abstain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go without' sounds like abstaining, but it tells PICKED to go outside L, the first letter of 'lieutenant'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickled is slang for intoxicated, like someone preserved in alcohol.

clue.text: Imagine very good cruet getting smashed

parts.note: PI, short for pious, means very good in crosswords

indicators.note: getting smashed says the word cruet is broken and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Picture a fine condiment set dropped and broken.
explanation.walkthrough: PI (pious) is crossword shorthand for very good; 'getting smashed' scrambles CRUET.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to form an image of it in the mind.

clue.text: Carefully study writing by one forced to enlist

parts.note: to con is an old word for studying closely
script means writing

explanation.surface: A recruit pores over the paperwork before signing up.
explanation.walkthrough: CON is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A conscript is someone compulsorily called up for military service.

clue.text: Are situated, for example, inside a Belgian city'

indicators.note: 'inside' puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: to lie is to be situated, as a town lies by a river
EG is short for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Things are placed, say, within a city in Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' only links the wordplay to the definition here.
explanation.definitionFit: Liège is a large city in eastern Belgium.

clue.text: They take turns to provide openings for entrants

definitions.text: They take turns to provide openings for entrants

parts.words: They take turns to provide openings for entrants
parts.note: read literally: objects that are turned by hand so that a way in opens for whoever is coming in

explanation.surface: Players alternate to give newcomers a chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take turns' sounds like alternating; here it means being twisted round, and 'openings' are doorways.
explanation.definitionFit: Handles on doors are rotated to open them and let people through.

clue.text: Claimed another examination

indicators.note: another signals a different version of the word Claimed, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone says they were owed a second check-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' asks for another arrangement of the letters of 'Claimed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical is a physical check-up by a doctor, a kind of examination.

clue.text: Meditated on seeing the doctor embracing poor Sue

indicators.note: embracing says the doctor's letters hold the other piece inside

parts.note: MD, doctor of medicine, is a doctor

indicators.note: poor signals the letters of Sue being put in a weaker, rearranged order

explanation.surface: Someone pondered while watching a physician hug an unfortunate woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' is the anagram signal, not pity: it reworks Sue's letters, and 'embracing' puts them inside the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to ponder or think deeply, so mused means meditated.

clue.text: Record by tired doctor is disgrace

parts.note: a disc is a record

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of tired are altered

explanation.surface: An exhausted physician's misdeed is a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is a verb here, tampering with TIRED to give REDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To discredit someone is to damage their good name, to bring shame on them.

clue.text: The head will be cold if he comes round

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: comes round signals the letters of if and he turning round into a new order

explanation.surface: The boss will be frosty if a man turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The head' is the definition, not a part of the wordplay; 'comes round' reworks the letters of 'if he' into HIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief is the leader of a group, its head.

clue.text: Lent a switch to some sailors for a lamp

indicators.note: switch tells the letters of Lent a to swap places

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, a body of sailors

explanation.surface: A light switch was loaned to a group of seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch' sounds like an electric switch, but it rearranges LENT A into LANTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp in a protective case.

clue.text: Ought to be in stem of boat

indicators.note: to be in tells the solver that one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a cane is a plant stem, as in sugar cane
ought, an old spelling of aught or nought, means nothing, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone insists a thing belongs at the front of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ought' looks like a verb, but it is the old word for nought, giving O, which goes inside CANE.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe is a light paddled vessel, so a type of boat.

clue.text: Outside broadcast term for a fixed idea

parts.note: OB is the standard abbreviation for an outside broadcast in television
a session is a term, as of a court or parliament

explanation.surface: A TV crew's location shoot becomes the name for a mania.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsession is an idea that grips the mind and will not go away.

clue.text: Stop nude members going outside unrestrained!

indicators.note: going outside tells the reworked letters to wrap round the other piece
the members, or parts, of the word nude are split up and rearranged

parts.note: to check is to stop or halt

explanation.surface: A naturist club parades outdoors with no one to rein them in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' breaks NUDE into UN and ED, which go outside CHECK.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unchecked has not been held back, so it runs free.

clue.text: Annoy fathead bringing in firearm

indicators.note: bringing in says the first word takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: to rile is to annoy
the head, or first letter, of fat is F

explanation.surface: An irritating idiot turns up carrying a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fathead' looks like an insult, but it is the head of 'fat', the letter F, placed inside RILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled gun, one kind of firearm.

clue.text: Expel about six, etc., when upset

indicators.note: when upset says the letters of the pieces are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
etc is written as it stands, the usual short form of et cetera

explanation.surface: A list of about six items and so on gets thrown out in disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when upset' scrambles VI and ETC; 'about' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To evict is to throw a tenant out, a way to expel someone.

clue.text: Fairly good food, which includes " role " spelt incorrectly!

indicators.note: which includes says the word for food holds the other piece inside

parts.note: table means food, as in keeping a good table

indicators.note: spelt incorrectly says the letters of role appear in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A passable meal whose menu misspells the word role.
explanation.walkthrough: TABLE means the food served, as in 'keeps a good table'; 'spelt incorrectly' gives OLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerable means acceptable or passable, so fairly good.

clue.text: Confused so dumb a person as one investigating grievances

indicators.note: confused says the letters of so dumb are muddled into a new order

parts.note: a man is a person

explanation.surface: Someone baffled and speechless is treated as a complaints official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' rearranges SO DUMB into OMBUDS; 'as' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ombudsman is an official appointed to look into complaints against organisations.

clue.text: .Save on offer for drinks, dispenser

parts.note: bar and save both mean except
to tender is to offer

explanation.surface: A discount on beverages is offered, perhaps from a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' means except here, as does BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A bartender serves drinks to customers at a bar.

clue.text: By chance I ordered manuscript about routine procedures

indicators.note: about tells the manuscript's letters to go round the other piece
ordered says the letters of chance I are arranged anew

explanation.surface: By luck someone requested a handwritten document on everyday methods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By chance' reads as a phrase, but only 'chance I' is reworked (giving ECHANIC); 'By' just links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The mechanics of something are its practical workings, the routine way it is done.

clue.text: Getting realist to change the betting system

indicators.note: to change asks for the letters of realist and to to be put in a different order

explanation.surface: A pragmatic punter decides to switch how they place bets.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'to' is part of the fodder as well as starting the anagram signal 'to change'; the pool is REALIST plus TO.
explanation.definitionFit: The totaliser, or tote, is the pool system that pays out winning bets on races.

clue.text: Harry buckled our new belt on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside says the reworked belt goes round the other piece
buckled means bent out of shape, so the letters of belt are rearranged
new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters of our

explanation.surface: Someone harassed fastens a fresh belt round their waist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' is the verb, to pester, not a name. 'buckled' gives TBLE and 'new' gives ROU.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry someone is to harass or worry them, to cause them bother.

clue.text: Said to strain stitches

indicators.note: said means the word for strain is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: to tax is to strain, as in taxing one's patience

explanation.surface: Someone claims sewing puts a strain on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' points to the sound: TAX, meaning strain, is spoken like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacks are long loose temporary stitches used in sewing.

clue.text: The sort that is surrounded by glasses!

indicators.note: surrounded by says the short form of that is goes inside the glasses

parts.note: specs is short for spectacles, glasses
IE, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A type of person found wearing spectacles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' gives IE, the abbreviation of Latin id est.
explanation.definitionFit: A species is a kind or type of thing.

clue.text: Different article in yellow case

indicators.note: case means the word for yellow forms a casing round the article

parts.note: or is the heraldic name for gold or yellow
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Something unusual sits in a yellow box.
explanation.walkthrough: In heraldry gold or yellow is called 'or'; 'case' makes it the container, and 'in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Other means not the same, so different.

clue.text: Half an hour to spend with the audience

indicators.note: half an points to the first half of the word hour

parts.note: to use is to spend, as in using up money

explanation.surface: Thirty minutes to pass in company with the spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half an' takes HO, the first half of 'hour'.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre's house is its audience, as in a full house.

clue.text: Canned brine mixture I consumed

indicators.note: mixture says the letters of brine and I are blended into a new order

parts.note: ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Tinned food in salt water, and I ate the lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canned' looks like the tin, but it is slang for drunk and is the definition. 'mixture' reorders BRINE as NEBRI, with I set before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Canned is slang for drunk, and an inebriate person is intoxicated.

clue.text: In it the rest is not suitable

indicators.note: in at the start says one piece goes inside the other word

parts.note: it is taken as it stands
a nap is a rest

explanation.surface: Lounging about here is inappropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' at the start looks like part of a phrase, but it is the container signal for the rest going inside 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means inappropriate or ill-fitting.

clue.text: Butts in with note, for a large quantity

indicators.note: in says the note goes inside the word for butts

parts.note: to ram is to butt, as a goat does
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Goats head-butting while singing, in great numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butts' is a verb here: RAMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Reams of something means a great deal, from a ream of paper.

clue.text: Mass murderer unhappy with a redhead in bed

parts.note: blue means sad or unhappy

indicators.note: in says the pieces before it go inside the word for bed

parts.note: bed is taken as it stands
the head, or first letter, of red is R

explanation.surface: A gloomy killer is found with a ginger-haired lover in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: A plus R, the head of 'red', go inside BED. Bluebeard is the wife-killer of the French folk tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluebeard is the folk-tale figure who murdered a series of wives.

clue.text: An excuse to bail out the Irish leader

indicators.note: out signals the letters of bail coming out of their usual order
leader points to the first letter of Irish

explanation.surface: Someone pleads a reason to post bail and free an Irish politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bail out' reads as a phrase, but 'out' rearranges BAIL; I is the leader of 'Irish'.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, often used loosely for any excuse.

clue.text: Trace note and allow the soldiers to' enter

parts.note: E is a musical note

indicators.note: to enter tells the soldiers to go inside the word for allow

parts.note: to let is to allow
men are soldiers, the ranks

explanation.surface: A message tells the guard to let the troops in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trace' is a noun here: a trace element, a tiny amount of a substance.
explanation.definitionFit: A trace or element of something is a small part or hint of it.

clue.text: Fights rises negotiated way back

indicators.note: negotiated signals the letters of rises being worked into a new order
back says the short word for way is read in reverse

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way

explanation.surface: A pay rise is bargained and someone fights their way back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiated' rearranges RISES to RESIS, and 'back' turns ST into TS.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to fight against something, so resists means fights.
